title: A Relationship Between Nonphysical Quasi-probabilities and Nonlocality Objectivity

candidates.exact_quote: A swap-intolerant nonlocal (SIN) state is a state ρ that is nonlocal, but whose qubit-swapped state ρ' is local.
candidates.claim_content: Setting: a 2-qubit density matrix is written ρ = (1/4)(I_4 + Σ_{i,j} c_{ij} σ_i ⊗ σ_j) with c_{ij} real and σ_i ∈ {I,X,Y,Z}. Let β be the 3×3 real matrix whose entries are the c_{ij} for which neither σ_i nor σ_j is the identity. The paper's Theorem 1.1 (Horodecki) states: ρ is nonlocal iff M := u + ū > 1, where u, ū are the two largest eigenvalues of β^T β. Definition 1.2 defines the qubit-swapped state ρ' = (1/4)(I_4 + Σ_{ij} c_{ij} σ_j ⊗ σ_i), i.e. the state whose correlation matrix is β^T (equivalently ρ' = SWAP·ρ·SWAP). The paper then asserts (Definition 1.3, Theorem 1.4) the existence of states with M(ρ) > 1 and M(ρ') ≤ 1. CLAIM TO CHECK: for any real 3×3 matrix β, the matrices β^T β and (β^T)^T β^T = β β^T have identical spectra, hence M(ρ') = M(ρ) for every state, and no state can be nonlocal under one qubit labelling and local under the other.
candidates.suspected_defect: The qubit swap sends β → β^T, so the Horodecki quantity for ρ' is the sum of the two largest eigenvalues of ββ^T, which has exactly the same eigenvalues as β^Tβ (AB and BA are isospectral; also ρ' = SWAP ρ SWAP is unitarily equivalent to ρ). Therefore M is invariant under the swap and swap-intolerant nonlocal states cannot exist, contradicting Definition 1.3 and Theorem 1.4, the paper's main result.

candidates.claim_content: β is the 3×3 real matrix with entries β_{jk} = c_{jk}, the coefficients of σ_j ⊗ σ_k with j,k ∈ {x,y,z} (no identities), in ρ = (1/4)(I_4 + Σ c_{ij} σ_i ⊗ σ_j). For a 'semi-trivial perp state' with defining point p = σ_i ⊗ I, the only nonzero entries of β are the row entries β_{ix}, β_{iy}, β_{iz} (the paper itself states that β has only one nonzero row or column). For p = I ⊗ σ_i the only nonzero entries are the column entries β_{xi}, β_{yi}, β_{zi}. The paper asserts that in the first case the eigenvalues/diagonal of β^T β are (β_{ix}^2, β_{iy}^2, β_{iz}^2) while in the second case they are (Σ_j β_{ji}^2, 0, 0). CHECK: if β has a single nonzero row v^T = (β_{ix}, β_{iy}, β_{iz}), compute β^T β explicitly: (β^T β)_{kl} = Σ_m β_{mk} β_{ml} = β_{ik} β_{il}, i.e. β^T β = v v^T, a rank-1 matrix with eigenvalues (|v|^2, 0, 0) = (β_{ix}^2 + β_{iy}^2 + β_{iz}^2, 0, 0).
candidates.suspected_defect: For a matrix with a single nonzero row, β^T β is the rank-one outer product v v^T, not a diagonal matrix with three nonzero entries. Its eigenvalues are (Σ_j β_{ij}^2, 0, 0) — identical in form to the p = I ⊗ i case. Hence the claimed 'asymmetry in β^T β' does not exist, and conditions (9) (which treat β_1^2, β_2^2, β_3^2 as three separate eigenvalues) and the subsequent construction of SIN states collapse.

candidates.exact_quote: one can construct a non-positive-semidefinite density state ρ whose smallest eigenvalue is λ₀
candidates.claim_content: The paper writes ρ = (1/4)(I_4 + Σ_{i,j} c_{ij} σ_i ⊗ σ_j) with Tr(ρ)=1, and quotes for perp states the eigenvalue formula λ(ρ) = 1 + c_p ± sqrt(Σ_pos (c_{i1}+c_{i2})^2 + Σ_neg (c_{i1}-c_{i2})^2) and λ(ρ) = 1 - c_p ± sqrt(Σ_pos (c_{i1}-c_{i2})^2 + Σ_neg (c_{i1}+c_{i2})^2), where c_p is the coefficient of the defining operator p and c_{i1}, c_{i2} are the coefficients of the two operators collinear with p in the i-th line. Test case: for p = Z⊗Z with only c_p = c nonzero, ρ = (1/4)(I + c Z⊗Z) has true eigenvalues (1+c)/4 (twice) and (1-c)/4 (twice), whereas the formula returns 1+c and 1-c. Thus the quantities in (6)/(7) are four times the actual eigenvalues of ρ (they sum to 4 rather than to Tr ρ = 1). In the proof of Theorem 1.4 the construction places E at distance |λ₀| outside the sphere (C, r_+), which makes the quantity '1 + τ_p − |E − C|' equal to λ₀; but the corresponding genuine eigenvalue of ρ is λ₀/4.
candidates.suspected_defect: The eigenvalue formula (6)/(7) omits the overall factor 1/4 of the density matrix; consequently the state constructed in Theorem 1.4 has smallest eigenvalue λ₀/4, not λ₀, so the theorem's quantitative statement is off by a factor of 4.

candidates.exact_quote: The semi-trivial perp state \( \rho \) is positive-semidefinite iff the state point \( E \) and its reflected point \( -E \) are contained on the surface or in the interior of the spheres \( (C, r_+) \), \( (C, r_-) \) respectively.
candidates.claim_content: For a semi-trivial perp state the paper gives the (unnormalised) eigenvalues as λ = 1 + τ_p ± sqrt(Σ_{i=1}^3 (β_i + τ_i)^2) and λ = 1 − τ_p ± sqrt(Σ_{i=1}^3 (β_i − τ_i)^2), where τ_p is the coefficient of the defining point p, E = (β_1, β_2, β_3) is the 'state point' formed by the coefficients of the operators in G_2, C = (τ_1, τ_2, τ_3) is the point formed by the partner coefficients, and r_± := 1 ± τ_p. Non-negativity of all four eigenvalues is therefore equivalent to |E + C| ≤ 1 + τ_p = r_+ and |E − C| ≤ 1 − τ_p = r_−. Proposition 2.1 instead asserts positivity is equivalent to |E − C| ≤ r_+ and |E + C| = |(−E) − C| ≤ r_−.
candidates.suspected_defect: The sphere assignments in Proposition 2.1 are swapped relative to the eigenvalue formula (7): (7) requires |E + C| ≤ r_+ and |E − C| ≤ r_−, while Proposition 2.1 states E must lie inside (C, r_+) (i.e. |E − C| ≤ r_+) and −E inside (C, r_−) (i.e. |E + C| ≤ r_−). For a fixed state these are different conditions (they differ by C → −C).

candidates.exact_quote: the eigenvalues are dependent upon the radii \( r_\pm \) and the distances \( |\pm E, C| \), so under translations and rotations of the parameter space \( S \), any eigenvalue-dependent property such as positive-definiteness is unchanged.
candidates.claim_content: A semi-trivial perp state is parameterised by τ_p, the state point E = (β_1,β_2,β_3) and the point C = (τ_1,τ_2,τ_3) in R^3 = S; its (unnormalised) eigenvalues are 1 + τ_p ± |E + C| and 1 − τ_p ± |E − C| (equivalently, by Prop. 2.1, they depend only on r_± = 1 ± τ_p and the distances |E − C| and |(−E) − C|). The paper claims that applying a translation of the parameter space S leaves all eigenvalue-dependent properties unchanged. CHECK: translating E ↦ E + t and C ↦ C + t gives |(E+t) − (C+t)| = |E − C| (unchanged) but |−(E+t) − (C+t)| = |E + C + 2t| ≠ |E + C| for t ≠ 0, because the reflected point of the translated state point is −(E+t), not (−E)+t.
candidates.suspected_defect: Translations of S are not symmetries of this parameterisation: the reflected point −E is determined by E, so a translation changes one of the two distances that determine the eigenvalues. Only rotations (and reflections) about the origin preserve both |E − C| and |E + C|. The claim as stated is false for translations.

candidates.exact_quote: Now for a given set of values for \( \tau_p,\, (\tau_i) = C \) one places \( C \) in the axis connecting \( E, -E \) (see Fig. 3). This provides the maximum distance \( E \) that leaves \( \rho \) positive semidefinite.
candidates.claim_content: Claim being proved: a semi-trivial perp state ρ, parameterised by τ_p, E = (β_1,β_2,β_3) and C = (τ_1,τ_2,τ_3), with positivity equivalent to the two sphere conditions |E ∓ C| ≤ 1 ± τ_p (radii r_± = 1 ± τ_p), cannot simultaneously be positive semidefinite and satisfy the nonlocality condition |E|^2 = Σ_i β_i^2 > 1. The proof step quoted asserts, without argument, that putting C on the line through E and −E maximises |E| subject to positivity, and then concludes from 2|E| = (1 + τ_p) + (1 − τ_p) = 2 that |E| ≤ 1.
candidates.suspected_defect: The optimality of placing C on the axis through E and −E is asserted, not proved; the paper also writes the equality 2|E| = 1 + τ_p + 1 − τ_p = 2 rather than an inequality. (The intended conclusion |E| ≤ 1 does follow directly from the triangle inequality 2|E| = |(E+C) + (E−C)| ≤ |E+C| + |E−C| ≤ 2, so the gap may be only presentational — but as written the key maximisation step is unjustified and the displayed relation is an equality where only an inequality holds.)

candidates.exact_quote: the boundary for nonlocality in general in this case (including swap-intolerant nonlocality) is the same as the boundary for positive semidefiniteness, identifying a boundary for physicality with one separating classical from quantum mechanics
candidates.claim_content: For semi-trivial perp states parameterised by τ_p, E = (β_1,β_2,β_3), C = (τ_1,τ_2,τ_3), the paper's own results give: (i) positivity ⟺ |E ∓ C| ≤ 1 ± τ_p for the specific C and τ_p of the state; (ii) nonlocality (left-identity labelling) ⟺ |E|^2 = Σβ_i^2 > 1. The paper concludes that the positive-semidefiniteness boundary coincides with the surface |E| = 1. CHECK: the condition |E| ≤ 1 is only a necessary consequence of positivity (derived via the triangle inequality); it is not sufficient. E.g. with τ_p = 0 and C = 0 one needs |E| ≤ 1, but choosing C far from the origin can make a state with |E| < 1 violate |E − C| ≤ 1 − τ_p and hence be non-positive.
candidates.suspected_defect: The set of positive-semidefinite semi-trivial perp states is a strict subset of {|E| ≤ 1}; the two boundaries do not coincide. Only the implication 'positive semidefinite ⇒ |E| ≤ 1' was established, so identifying the positivity boundary with the sphere |E| = 1 overstates what was proved.

candidates.exact_quote: A 2-qubit density matrix \( \rho \) describes a nonlocal state iff the matrix \( \beta \) of coefficients of maximally mixed operators obeys the following:
candidates.claim_content: The paper states as an 'iff' that a 2-qubit density matrix ρ is nonlocal exactly when M = u + ū > 1, where u, ū are the two largest eigenvalues of β^Tβ and β is the 3×3 correlation matrix (coefficients of σ_i ⊗ σ_j with both σ's nontrivial). The Horodecki result actually characterises violation of the CHSH inequality: max_CHSH = 2 sqrt(u + ū), so M > 1 ⟺ the state violates CHSH. There exist 2-qubit mixed states that admit no local hidden variable model for general measurements (or are nonlocal under other Bell inequalities) yet satisfy M ≤ 1.
candidates.suspected_defect: The 'iff' is stated for nonlocality in general, whereas the Horodecki criterion is necessary and sufficient only for CHSH violation. The paper's conclusions about 'local' swapped states therefore only concern CHSH-nonlocality.

candidates.exact_quote: we let |E| = 1 + ½|λ₀| - outside the unit sphere in S thus giving a nonlocal state
candidates.claim_content: In the paper's own framework (Eq. (8) and conditions (9)), the Horodecki quantity for a semi-trivial perp state is M = Σ_j β_{ji}^2 when p = I ⊗ i (so M > 1 ⟺ |E| > 1), but M = (sum of the two largest of β_1^2, β_2^2, β_3^2) when p = i ⊗ I, in which case |E| > 1 does NOT imply M > 1. The proof of Theorem 1.4 asserts that |E| = 1 + ½|λ₀| > 1 'thus gives a nonlocal state' without specifying the labelling, and the construction later requires the right-identity labelling to be local.
candidates.suspected_defect: Under the paper's own Eq. (8), 'outside the unit sphere ⇒ nonlocal' holds only for the left-identity labelling p = I ⊗ i; the inference as stated is a non sequitur for p = i ⊗ I, precisely the case the construction needs to be local.
